hero.title: Biotechnology in Italy
hero.subtitle: Study Biotechnology in Italy at renowned research universities specializing in medical biotechnology, pharmaceutical genomics, and industrial bio-applications. Indian students gain extensive hands-on laboratory experience and internationally recognized qualifications under the European ECTS framework.

highlights.eligibility: Recognised academic qualification + English / Italian proficiency

overview: Italy is a popular destination for students looking to pursue a course in biotechnology, molecular biology, genetics, pharmaceutical research and other branches of science. Italian universities offer courses which combine classroom learning, laboratory training and research. Students can learn about the application of biotechnology in healthcare, agriculture, medicine, pharmaceuticals and environmental science.

Biotechnology in Italy is a good option for students who want to learn how living organisms and biological processes can be used to develop medicines, improve agriculture, support scientific research and create sustainable industrial solutions.
Students can study for a bachelor degree, a master program or a PhD, depending on their educational background and career goals.

Indian students get a chance to experience European education, learn advanced scientific techniques and explore international research opportunities when they study Biotechnology in Italy . Some master programs are completely in English, and many bachelor programs are in Italian.
Edu-Hawk Worldwide helps students find the right university for them, understand the admission requirements, prepare application documents, and plan their study abroad journey.

items: Italy offers a wide range of biotechnology programs for students with an interest in biology, medicine, pharmaceutical research, industrial applications and environmental science.
Below are some reasons why you should study biotechnology in Italy.

Education with a research focus: Students are introduced to scientific concepts, laboratory techniques and research methodologies, enabling them to comprehend how biotechnology functions in practical settings.
Diverse Specializations: Students can select their area of interest from medical, pharmaceutical, molecular, industrial, agricultural and environmental biotechnology.
Master's Programs in English Many Italian universities offer master's programs in English, which are perfect for international students who do not speak Italian.
Practical experience in the lab: Depending on the university and the program, students may get the opportunity to gain hands-on experience through lab work, research projects and internships.
Interdisciplinary Learning Biotechnology is a blend of biology, chemistry, genetics, microbiology, bioinformatics and other sciences.
International Study Experience: Students will have the opportunity to study in a multicultural environment, meet people from different countries and experience European academic life.
Scholarships and financial aid: Eligible students can look for university scholarships, local financial aid, and lower tuition.

Students planning to Study Biotechnology in Italy should compare course subjects, teaching language, laboratory facilities, research opportunities and future career options before choosing a university.
Italian universities offer a range of biotechnology programs to cater for students from different educational backgrounds and career aspirations.
Bachelor of Biotechnology
A bachelor's degree in biotechnology is usually completed in 3 years and generally consists of 180 ECTS credits.
During the course students will learn about:
Cell Biology
Molecular Biology
Heredity
Microbiology and
Biochemistry
Chemistry
Techniques in the lab
Applications of Biotechnology
These subjects help students learn about the biological processes and the application of biotechnology in different industries.
Some of the Italian bachelor's programs are in Italian.
For example, the University of Bologna offers a three-year bachelor's in Biotechnology taught in Italian. The program has limited access through TOLC-I for the academic year 2026/27.
Applicants are advised to check the latest admission requirements and university notices before applying.
Biotechnology, M.S.
A master's degree in biotechnology typically lasts 2 years and usually consists of 120 ECTS credits.
Students can select a specialization according to their interests and previous studies.
Popular specializations are:
Biotech Medical
Biotech Pharmaceuticals
Industry Biotechnology
Biotechnology Molecular
Biotechnology & Bioinformatics
Biotechnology for the Bio-economy
Agriculture Biotechnology
Environmental Biotechnology
Students seeking English-taught programs may have more options at master's than at bachelor's level.
However, the language of instruction, the eligibility conditions and the admission procedure are dependent on the university and the program.
Biotechnology Doctoral Programs
If you are a student who wants to go for higher studies and work in advanced scientific research, you might want to consider a PhD in biotechnology.
Research areas could include:
Cell and Molecular Biology
Genetic Engineering
Drug Development
Research in Drugs and Medical
Industrial bioprocesses
Biotechnology in Agriculture and Environment
A PhD normally requires a relevant master's degree.
Some universities require students to submit a research proposal, attend an interview or complete a selection process.

When comparing Biotechnology Courses in Italy , students should consider if they want to specialize in laboratory research, pharmaceutical development, bioinformatics, industrial applications or academic research.
3. Best Biotechnology Universities in Italy
Several universities in Italy offer biotechnology-related programs.
Students are advised to look at the most recent course offerings, language of instruction, admission requirements and application deadlines prior to selecting a university.
1. Università di Bologna
For those interested in a career in medical, pharmaceutical and industrial research, the University of Bologna offers various biotechnology programs.
The following programs are relevant for the academic year 2026/27:
Biotechnology:
Three-year bachelor's program taught in Italian Limited admission
Medical Biotechnology:
A two-year master program taught entirely in English.
Pharmaceutical and Industrial Biotechnology:
A two year master program fully taught in English.
Medical biotechnology refers to the use of biotechnology in healthcare, biomedical research and diagnostics.
Pharmaceutical and Industrial Biotechnology deals with pharmaceutical products, industrial processes and production based on biotechnology.
These programs might be appropriate for students who want to develop scientific knowledge and practical skills in biotechnology.
Official course info: https://www.unibo.it/en/study
2. Milan University
The University of Milan has bachelor and master level programs in biotechnology.
Relevant Master's programs are:
Medical and Molecular Biotechnology
Molecular Biotechnology and Bioinformatics
Biotechnology to Bioeconomy

Medical Biotechnology and Molecular Medicine is a two-year master's program that is taught in English, according to the university's course catalog for 2026/27. Enrollment is limited and there is an admission test
Molecular Biotechnology and Bioinformatics is also a two-year master's program, taught in English.
These programs may be suitable for students interested in molecular biology, medical research, computational biology, industrial biotechnology and sustainable biological production.
Official course info: https://www.unimi.it/en/education
3. University of Rome - Tor Vergata
Master's program in Biotechnology for Industry and Health - University of Rome Tor Vergata
The program is a two-year degree entirely taught in English for the academic year 2026/27.
Students need a relevant bachelor's degree and the academic requirements of the university.
The university will examine the student's prior subject areas, academic preparation, and credit requirements in appropriate areas of biological science.
Students who want to learn about biotechnology and its uses in health and industry may be interested in this program.
Official course info: https://biotechnology.uniroma2.it/
Selecting the Best University
Students should compare before selecting a university:
Degree level and length of study

- Subjects of the course and academic credits
Entrance test and selection procedure

The right university depends on your previous education, preferred specialization and future career goals.

sections.title: Who can study Biotechnology in Italy?

items: Admission requirements for biotechnology programs differ depending on the university, degree level and specialization.
Bachelor Degree Requirements
For a bachelor's degree, students generally need:
An accepted secondary school qualification which meets the requirements for entry to an Italian university.
Academic preparation in subject areas, as appropriate, such as biology, chemistry and mathematics.
English or Italian language proficiency as required by the program.
Entrance Test / Selection Process (as per the university)
Students are advised to check that their school qualification is accepted by the university before applying.
Master's Degree Requirements
Students who want a master's degree generally need:
A recognized first degree in biotechnology, biology, biochemistry, life sciences or a comparable field acceptable to the University.
Relevant college credits in biology, chemistry, genetics or other required subjects.
Adequate academic preparation for the chosen program.
English language proficiency (if applicable) for English-taught programs.
Entrance test, interview or other assessment, if needed.
For example, the master's degree in Biotechnology for Industry and Health at Tor Vergata expects students to have a relevant academic background and to meet the university's curriculum requirements.
Students who have relevant degrees may be required to demonstrate that they have taken the required subjects and have the required academic credits.
PhD Requirements
A relevant master's degree is normally required for students applying for a PhD.
Depending on the program they may also need:
Previous research background
A plan for research
Letters of recommendation from academic referees
Interview
Other documents as required by the University
Indian students should verify that their previous qualifications meet the requirements of the university before starting the application process.
Italian universities select students on the basis of their academic background, previous subjects, language skills and suitability to the program chosen.
Standard admission requirements are:
Recognized educational qualifications
Academic studies marksheets and transcripts
Master's application bachelor's degree certificate
Knowledge of English or Italian, where required
CV for relevant post-graduate programs
Statement of Purpose or motivation letter, if needed
Where appropriate, letters of recommendation
Entrance examination results if applicable
Attendance for any interview where applicable
Official translation of educational documents, if required
Further qualification documents requested by the university
Each university has different entry requirements.

Some universities will take students with relevant scientific backgrounds, whereas others will require a specific degree or a minimum number of credits in subjects such as biology, chemistry and genetics.
Edu-Hawk Worldwide assists students in understanding university requirements, organizing their documents and developing an application plan based on their educational background.
The cost of studying biotechnology in Italy depends on the university, the particular course, its fee structure, and the financial aid available.
Some public universities determine tuition based on the student's financial status and university regulations. Private institutions generally have their own fee structure.
Estimated Tuition Fees Per Year
University Type Approximate Tuition fee per year Approximate INR Equivalent
Public Universities €900 - €4000 ₹97,200 - ₹4,32,000
These numbers are general planning estimates for higher education in Italy. These are not confirmed fees for all the biotechnology program.
The actual tuition fees may vary up or down according to the university and the program.
Example conversion: 1€ = ₹108.
The INR amounts are indicative and may vary based on the exchange rate.
Estimated monthly cost of living
Also, students should also plan their monthly expenses while studying in Italy.
Expense Monthly Cost Estimate
Accommodation: 300-600 €
Food & Groceries €150-€250
Local transport €25-60
Utilities and Personal Expenses €100-€200
Total Estimated €700-€1,100
Indicative monthly cost of living in the example exchange rate is between ₹75,600-₹1,18,800.
Actual costs depend on the city, type of accommodation, your personal lifestyle and spending habits.
Scholarships and Financial Aid
For example, students may investigate different funding support options:
University merit scholarships
Scholarships and financial aids in the region
Reduction/exemption of tuition fees
Funding for research in eligible doctoral programs.
Each scholarship has its own criteria, application deadlines and documentation requirements.
Scholarships and financial aid are not guaranteed.
To be able to calculate the Biotechnology Fees in Italy, one should include tuition fees, accommodation, food, insurance, travel, visa-related expenses and other living costs.
Always check the latest university fee schedule before you accept an admission offer.

items: There are many career opportunities in biotechnology and the professional requirements vary depending on the job, the employer and the country where students want to work.
Research Career
Relevant degrees, laboratory experience and further postgraduate qualifications may be required for specialist positions for research students.
Pharmaceutical Industry Background
The pharmaceutical industry might want to know about laboratory procedures, drug development, quality control and pharmaceutical production.
Bio-informatics
Students interested in studying bioinformatics may require additional skills in programming, statistics, data analysis and computational biology.
Quality Control and Quality Assurance
These positions may require knowledge of laboratory testing, documentation, quality standards, and industry practices.
Regulated Health Professions
A biotechnology degree does not automatically entitle students to work as doctors, pharmacists or other regulated healthcare professionals.
Additional education, licensing, or professional registration may be required.
Employment in India
Students planning to return to India should refer to the requirements of their prospective employer and any relevant professional or regulatory body.
Before joining, students should be aware of whether the chosen degree is aligned with their educational and career goals.

Pharmaceutical companies, research laboratories, biotechnology industries, universities, healthcare-related industries, agriculture and environmental technology are some of the career opportunities for biotechnology graduates.
Your opportunities will depend on your degree, your practical experience and technical skills, and the area in which you have specialized.
Career Opportunities
Biotechnologist: Works on biological systems and biotechnology applications in various sectors.
Research Assistant/Research Associate: Support scientific research, laboratory experiments and research projects.
Laboratory Analyst Conducts laboratory tests, analyzes samples and prepares scientific reports.
Molecular Biology Technician - Works with biological samples using molecular biology techniques.
Pharmaceutical Research Associate: Assists with pharmaceutical research, drug development and laboratory work.
Quality Control Analyst: Examines products, samples and lab results to ensure quality standards are maintained.
Quality Assurance Associate : Assists in the maintenance of quality procedures, documentation and adherence to industry requirements.
Bioinformatics Analyst: They work with biological data and computational tools, depending on their technical skills.
Bioprocess or Industrial Biotechnology Associate: Assists with industrial production, fermentation and biotech processes.
Clinical Research Support Professional : Supports clinical research activities and associated paperwork.
Associate in Agricultural or Environmental Biotechnology: Works with biotechnology applications in agriculture, sustainability and environmental sciences.
Industries using biotechnology graduates
Pharmaceuticals and Health Care: Biotechnology graduates can work in research, drug development, diagnostics and biotechnology-based products.
Research and Academia: Laboratory research, scientific projects and higher education are possible career paths.
Industrial Biotechnology: Graduates may work in production optimization and quality control, fermentation and bioprocessing.
Agriculture and Environment: Biotechnology can be applied in crop science, sustainable production, environmental monitoring and bio-remediation.
Bioinformatics and Data Science : Students who have the right computational skills can work on biological data analysis and computational research.
Your opportunities will be dependent on your academic qualifications, practical experience, technical knowledge, language skills and work authorization.
Students interested in specialized research positions may find a Master's degree or PhD helpful.

For students studying biotechnology in Italy , the focus should be on the development of laboratory skills, research experience, data analysis capabilities, and scientific communication to improve their career prospects.

faq.question: Can Indian students pursue a degree in biotechnology in Italy?
faq.answer: Yes, Indian students can apply for biotechnology courses in eligible Italian universities . Students must meet the academic eligibility, language proficiency and documentation requirements of the university of their choice. Admission is subject to the selection process of the program and previous qualifications of the student.

faq.question: Are biotechnology courses in English in Italy?
faq.answer: Yes, there are some biotechnology master programs that are fully taught in English. English taught options are available for selected programs at the University of Bologna, University of Milan and University of Rome Tor Vergata. But most degree courses are in Italian. Applicants should ensure the language of instruction is correct when applying.

faq.question: What are the biotechnology fees in Italy?
faq.answer: Tuition fees vary by university, program and applicable fee rules. As a general planning estimate public university fees may range from €900 to €4,000 per year. However, fees for individual biotechnology courses may vary. Students should refer to the current university fee schedule for the exact cost.

faq.question: Is a biology degree a good fit for a masters in biotechnology?
faq.answer: Yes, a biology bachelors degree can be a good fit for some masters programs in biotechnology. But the eligibility depends on the university. Some universities will accept students with a related life-science background, while others require a certain number of credits in biology, chemistry, genetics or other subjects. Students are advised to check the programme's curriculum requirements before applying.

faq.question: What to do after studying biotechnology in Italy?
faq.answer: After studying biotechnology, students can look for jobs in research, pharmaceuticals, laboratory analysis, quality control, industrial biotechnology, bioinformatics, agriculture and environmental biotechnology.
